title: Derivation of the Fine-Structure Constant from Dx Theory
content: This article presents a geometric completion of gravitational and quantum mechanics within the Dx framework. We re-evaluate the fabric of matter, defining it as a dual complex wave function composed of a Space Fraction (ρ, governing mass and potential energy) and a Time Fraction (ϕ, governing frequency and kinetic energy). The universal vacuum flux (Ξ_vac) is the fundamental precursor to all forces; electromagnetism and gravity are simply different manifestations of how this flux twists or gets obstructed across different dimensions.When matter approaches an extreme gravitational region like a Schwarzschild black hole, it undergoes a discrete Z₂ symmetry transition at a clear boundary. Instead of collapsing into an infinitely dense point (a classical singularity), the physical mass is decelerated by an inverted, repulsive dynamic force, establishing a strict kinematic entry throttle of v_entry = αc. Within this non-singular halted core, the translational momentum of opposing helical waves locks into a stationary state, cleanly separating the space and time fractions. By evaluating the precise topological phase-space volumes required to execute this 1D transition gate (π), anchor the 3D stationary core (π²), and unitarily store the background kinetic flux in an orthogonal 4D Hilbert space (4π³), we derive the low-energy fine-structure constant (1/α ≈ 137.036) directly from pure geometry.Crucially, this framework mathematically forbids matter from accelerating to  as it crosses the horizon. The geometric throttle of the  boundary restricts the entry velocity of infalling matter to exactly  . We present a direct observational challenge to the astrophysics community: re-evaluate recent X-ray spectra from the plunging regions inside the ISCO.
